bug_semantics: An authenticated student could request a teacher-only course URL with a user-controlled course ID. The analytics page hid its navigation item from students but still called a server endpoint that accepted that course ID, used the Supabase service-role client, and returned course membership/profile data, lesson and exercise totals, progress, grades/submissions-derived statistics, and last-login data without enforcing an admin/tutor role. Client-side hiding therefore did not protect the privileged read and produced the advisory's transient disclosure; the same UI-only authorization pattern affected the other named course pages.
flaw_origin: The first member of PR #574, 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3, newly added the role-hidden analytics navigation item, the unguarded analytics page, and the service-role POST endpoint keyed only by request-supplied courseId. The public mainline commit ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817 is the squash aggregate of that PR and is not the BIC; the member commit is the smallest commit that first wrote this concrete vulnerable data path.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 shows human author and committer emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com>, subject 'feat: added anaytics for the course page', an empty body, and no AI-tool trailer, bot identity, Co-Authored-By line, or other AI marker.
evidence: The assigned GHSA-mh75-3225-9wcj/CVE-2025-65670 advisory identifies ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and unauthorized sensitive course/admin/student disclosure after a student manipulates course IDs in teacher/admin URLs. At the affected tag, the analytics route sends the URL-derived course ID to a server-side analytics read that exposes roster/profile and progress information.

Introducer disagreement resolved against the primary's 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b and for the reviewer's 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3. git grep at 07eba6b's parent 220f35b3db55f46bc42519b9e82d481c8325a3d6 already finds fetchCourse(courseId) in attendance/people/submissions and fetchSubmissions in the submissions route and service; git show 07eba6b adds RoleBasedSecurity/client hiding around already existing reads, so it did not first write the vulnerable data path. In contrast, git diff-tree reports both apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts and apps/dashboard/src/routes/courses/[id]/analytics/+page.svelte as A in 4198d15, and git show displays the new service-role endpoint, request-supplied courseId, unguarded page call, and hidden-from-students navigation together. This is a focused creation, not an import, move, refactor, or aggregate.

History checks independently select the reviewer BIC: git log -S 'const { courseId } = await request.json();' b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505 -- apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts returns only 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3, and git log -L 11,16 on that path shows the handler entering from /dev/null in that commit.

Parent disagreement resolved for 7d150ea5004f466e35d839b6344580866f855abe, not 220f35b3db55f46bc42519b9e82d481c8325a3d6. git cat-file -p 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 names 7d150ea5004f466e35d839b6344580866f855abe as its sole immediate parent, and git cat-file -e '7d150ea5004f466e35d839b6344580866f855abe:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts' fails because the path does not exist. The BIC diff creates both endpoint and page from /dev/null, establishing parent absence directly.

Squash decomposition is verified locally rather than selecting the mainline aggregate: git rev-list --parents from b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505 yields the seven listed PR members back to 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 (including the recorded merge member), and git rev-parse shows b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505^{tree} and squash landing ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817^{tree} are both 25968dd2ef62d6ce96cd75355e4cd94b08161a87.

Affected-version boundary: git tag --contains ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817 includes releases beginning v0.1.2, the advisory's v0.1.13, and 0.2.11. The branch-only member is linked to those releases through the verified equal-tree squash landing rather than incorrectly treating the aggregate as the BIC.

Fix disagreement resolved against the primary's ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e and for the reviewer's 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052. git show ac1a05f reveals an 80%-similarity endpoint rename plus a check assigning the UserPermissionResult object from checkUserCoursePermissions to hasPermission and testing if (!hasPermission); git show ac1a05f:apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/functions/permissions.ts proves the helper always returns an object containing hasAccess/isStudent, so the condition is never false for a student or nonmember. git show 0.2.11:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/courses/analytics/+server.ts retains that ineffective object-as-boolean check, proving 0.2.10/ac1a05f is not a complete fix.

The minimal direct repair is b4326e6517e0b9f058dfe86c173b0c10d58c3b35: git show replaces courseMemberMiddleware, which permits students, with courseTeamMemberMiddleware on GET /:courseId/analytics. git rev-parse gives the same course.ts blob e8bd5c9f22bc575fca708769c968ace65ef5b6c6 at b4326e6517e0b9f058dfe86c173b0c10d58c3b35 and its mainline squash landing 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052. git tag --contains 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 begins at v0.3.0, while git tag --contains ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e includes still-vulnerable 0.2.10 and 0.2.11; therefore v0.3.0 is the verified first fixed tag.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file -p 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 contains only a human author/committer and ordinary feature subject with no AI marker. Cursor Agent authored the later direct fix, but fix-only AI evidence is excluded by protocol and does not change the BIC verdict.
reasoning: The reviewer wins all three assigned core disagreements. The primary's introducer is an attempted client-side gate layered over reads already present in its parent, so it is neither the first writer of the concrete vulnerable sink nor the smallest BIC. The reviewer instead decomposed the analytics squash and identified the focused member that simultaneously created the privileged service-role endpoint, attacker-controlled course-ID request, unguarded page invocation, and UI-only hiding; its commit object and immediate parent directly establish the BIC and parent. The primary's proposed terminal fix is also ineffective because it treats a structured permission result as a boolean, a defect still present in 0.2.11. The reviewer direct fix enforces the intended team-member role at the API boundary, its exact file blob landed in 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052, and v0.3.0 is the first containing tag. With a verified BIC, absent parent mechanism, verified repair/version boundary, and no BIC commit-object AI signal, the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
